about: Every setting a saved style can carry, once, under its saved name. Written by tools/settings-list.mjs from presets.js, the new window (plugin/assets/js/panel-window.js: page, section, row, changesPage), plugin/words.php, tools/split_style.py and functions.php. It is also a source: presets.js's tables (DIALS, OPTS, the lists, PICKS, LEVELS, ROLES, ROLE_DEFAULT, MEMBERS, the aliases, the meanings) are a block written from it, and split_style.py reads REST (rest, restValues) and ABSENT from it. Change a table here and run node tools/settings-list.mjs. A setting's label (the word the window shows) is kept by hand here. {role}, {member} and {side} stand for the ids in roles and sides.

means.roles: Typography by seven roles, named for their job and tied to the HTML every site has. title: the one big line of a page (h1, the post title). headings: the headings inside the text (h2 to h6) and the site's name. body: what people read (p, li). quote: quotations. meta: small facts around the text (dates, authors, categories, tags, captions). interface: menus, buttons, fields, labels. code: code, pre, kbd. Every role takes font, size, weight, lineHeight, letterSpacing, capitals, italic; title and headings also align; every role also takes a colour (text, mutedText, accent or own). A dial left out is the theme's own. size is a step from the role's own size (-4 to +6, each 1.125 apart). lineHeight: tight, snug, normal, relaxed, loose. letterSpacing: tighter, tight, normal, wide, wider, widest. Records say architrave 3 (2 before the seven colours); older records with the eight roles are read into the seven.
means.colours: Seven colours per side, named for their job, as hex: background (Paper: the page the text sits on), background2 (Ground: the space around the page and the rails, a theme's second background), card (Cards: menus, boxes, fields standing on the page), text, mutedText (Soft text: dates, captions, small facts), accent (the brand colour: links and the main buttons) and highlight (the highlighter's colour; left out, none). Beside them the button's own colour and each type role's own (title, headings, body, quote, meta, interface, code), used with button own and roles.<role>.colour own. Leave out what you do not need: the rest is mixed from background and text. text on background must reach 4.5:1 and accent on background 3:1 on both sides. A background2 on the other side of its background (dark around a light page, light around a dark one) is a dark ground, worn around the page on wide screens with its own words, lines and links. Older records name paper, ink, ground, lift and marker; they are read as these. primary, foreground and muted-foreground are read as accent, text and mutedText.
means.effects: The extras' details, one object per effect (title, serif, arrival, cardlight, moving, button, pattern, guides, tint, aurora, pointer, dividers, topline, picglow), each holding only the details that differ from their rest; the effect's own switch is its flat pick (titlefinish, headitalics, headarrival, cardlight, buttonfinish, toppattern, guides, greytint, pageglow, movinglight) or, for the last four, its look.

roles.label: Title
roles.where: The one big line of a page: the article's title, a page's name.

roles.label: Headings
roles.where: The headings inside the text, and the site's name.

roles.label: Reading text
roles.where: What people read: paragraphs, lists, excerpts, the comments' words.

roles.label: Small text
roles.where: Small facts around the text: dates, authors, categories, tags, captions, names in comments.

roles.label: Interface
roles.where: The site around the text: menus, buttons, fields, labels, section titles.

roles.label: Code
roles.where: Code and keys, inline and in blocks.

means.font: A face id from the list, or body / interface to follow the reading or the interface font. Left out: the theme's own.
means.size: Steps from the role's own size, each 1.125 times the one before: -1 a little smaller, +1 a little larger, +3 about half again as large. 0 or left out: the theme's own.
means.weight: thin 100 to black 900; a face offers the weights it has and falls to the nearest.
means.lineHeight: tight for big titles, snug for headings, normal is the theme's own, relaxed for long reading, loose for airy small text.
means.letterSpacing: tighter and tight close large type up, normal is the theme's own, wide to widest open small capitals and labels.
means.capitals: true sets the role in capitals.
means.italic: true sets it in italic, where the face has one.
means.align: default (the start), center or right; title and headings.
means.colour: text (the text colour), mutedText (Soft text, the quiet colour of dates and captions), accent (the brand colour), or own (the role's own colour, colours.<side>.<role>). Left out: text, and for meta mutedText.

settings.means: Always 1. Marks the JSON as a style record.
The name on the tile.
The built-in style this record starts from; every key left out rests on it. See examples for what each base is.
The reading size step of the article, a fluid rung and not a pixel value; default is about 22px on a desktop. Do not set a size for a monospaced reading face, its phone floor is handled by the theme.
settings.label: Reading size

settings.means: Justified paragraphs with hyphenation.
settings.label: Justified text

settings.means: A large initial on the first paragraph; capLines is its height in lines.
settings.label: Drop cap

settings.means: Inter's alternate letters: the one with a longer flag, round quotes, commas and apostrophes. Only while the interface face is Inter; the article keeps its own face's letters.
settings.label: Alternate letters

settings.means: Legacy. The theme always applies paragraph settings everywhere.
settings.label: Where paragraph settings apply

settings.means: Height of the initial in lines. Only with dropcap.
settings.label: Drop cap height

settings.means: Where the line of categories stands on the article and on its cards: below the title (the rest), above it, or hidden. It replaced the switch kickerabove.
settings.label: Categories

settings.means: How the tags at the end of an article look: text (the rest: words, as the theme sets them), or small pills that are filled, tinted, gray or outlined, made from the button colour. Tags follow the buttons gives the pills the buttons' corner.
settings.label: Tags

settings.means: How cards and boxes look: the theme's cards (link cards, the support box) and a box the writer coloured in an article (a Group block with a background): filled (the rest: the card's own fill, no line, whatever the Lines slider), outlined (a line on the paper, as wide as the Lines slider says, never under 1 px; a coloured box keeps its colour) or raised (lifted by a shadow).
settings.label: Cards

settings.means: How quotes look, in an article and as a quote post: sideLine (set in, with a vertical line at the side, whatever the lines setting; the rest on Architrave), indented (set in from the edge, no line; the rest on another theme), plain (the words alone, not set in) or filled (in a box with its fill and no line, whatever the Lines slider; a quote post's card). Quotes are italic.
settings.label: Quotes

settings.means: How search, comment and sign-up fields look: filled (the rest: the fill, no line, whatever the Lines slider), outlined (a line on the paper, as wide as the Lines slider says) or raised (lifted by a shadow).
settings.label: Fields

settings.means: Paragraphs spaced apart (the rest) or indented with no space between, as print sets them.
settings.label: Between paragraphs

settings.means: The drop cap's letter: text (the rest, the reading text's own face and weight), bold (the reading face in bold, as the title), fraunces (a soft old-style display capital) or title (the heading role's own face, weight, slant and colour). Shows with Drop cap on.
settings.label: Drop cap font

settings.means: Where words break at the line's end: auto (the rest: with Justified text, every word that may), few (long words only, on any edge, never on two lines in a row), any (every word that may, on any edge) or off (never).
settings.label: Hyphens

settings.means: The article's first paragraph speaks up, as a launch page opens on one big sentence: off (the rest) or big (1.4 times the text, medium, in the ink). Architrave's page only.
settings.label: Opening sentence

settings.means: How links in the text are marked: both (the rest: the accent and an underline), coloured (the accent alone, no underline even under the pointer), underlined (the ink with a quiet underline), bold (the ink on a thick underline in the accent, filled with the accent under the pointer) or wash (the ink on a pale wash of the accent, as a highlighter lays it, filled with the accent under the pointer). Not set, a style with soft marks them underlined, and an export leaves it out.
settings.label: Links

settings.means: A fine line around pictures without a frame, so a white screenshot keeps its edge on a white paper: none (the rest), faint (the ink at 8 %), medium (16 %) or strong (30 %), drawn inside the picture. Architrave's page only.
settings.label: Picture edge
problems: the word 'Picture edge' is in neither plugin/words.php nor architrave_settings_words()

settings.means: How many letters a line of reading text holds: 60 to 88 in steps of 4; 72 is the theme's own (45 to 75 is the classic range for comfortable reading). The column grows with the text size. On another theme it sets the theme's content width.
settings.label: Line length

settings.means: How wide the article's title, categories and date stand: content (the reading column, the rest) or wide (the theme's wide width, as the wide top picture). WordPress's own words. Architrave's page only.
settings.label: Title width

settings.means: How wide the article's first picture stands: content (the reading column, the rest), wide (the theme's wide width) or full (edge to edge across the paper, a low 21:9 banner with square corners). WordPress's own words. Architrave's page only.
settings.label: Picture width

settings.means: How wide the pictures inside the article stand: content (the reading column, the rest) or wide (as the wide top picture, centred, with more air). Architrave's page only.
settings.label: Pictures in the text

settings.means: The corners of cards, buttons, fields and pictures: none (square), small, medium (the theme's own), large or xlarge. One step re-cuts every corner together; corners inside corners stay sums.
settings.label: Corners

settings.means: How wide every line is: the lines between rows, around buttons and the line of an outlined card, quote or field. none (the theme's own: no lines but link underlines), hairline (half a pixel), or 1, 2, 3 or 5 px. It adds no line to a filled box: that is the Cards, Quotes and Fields rows' choice.
settings.label: Lines

settings.means: solid (the rest), dashed or dotted lines. Dashes are long only with radius none. Only with a borderWidth.
settings.label: Line style

settings.means: How strong the lines are: the text colour's share in the line colour, 10, 20, 45 (the theme's own), 70 or 100 per cent. Only with a borderWidth.
settings.label: Line strength

settings.means: What fills the main buttons: accent (the brand colour, the rest), text, or own (colours.<side>.button). The links keep the accent either way.
settings.label: Colour

settings.means: The buttons' corners: match (the corners every card has, the rest), square, rounded (8 px) or pill. Only with a radius.
settings.label: Corners

settings.means: How the main buttons look (the one action, like Subscribe): filled (the rest), outlined, shadow (outlined with a hard shadow), tinted, gray or text (text only), in the button colour.
settings.label: Main

settings.means: How the other buttons look (a second choice beside the main one): gray (the rest), filled, tinted, outlined, shadow or text, in the button colour where it has one.
settings.label: Other

settings.means: How the quiet buttons look (small actions, like Share): text (the rest), filled, tinted, gray, outlined or shadow. Architrave's alone; another theme has no quiet kind.
settings.label: Quiet

settings.means: true: the tags' pills take the buttons' corner instead of staying round.
settings.label: Tags match buttons

settings.means: How the current item is marked (the page you are on in the menu, the open tab): gray (the rest: the theme's own mark), filled with the button colour, outlined in it, or bold and underlined.
settings.label: Current item

settings.means: How every image on the site is shown: none (as published, the rest), grayscale, sepia, tinted (in the colour pair's paper and text), duotone (paper and accent), grain (film grain), warm, or hidden (no pictures).
settings.label: Picture look

settings.means: true: the picture look lifts under the pointer and the real colours show. Nothing with pictureFilter none or hidden.
settings.label: Colour on hover

settings.means: true: pictures are dimmed a little on the dark side.
settings.label: Dim in dark appearance

settings.means: The frame around pictures: none (a picture stands on the paper with its corner alone), plain (a mat in the fields' colour, the rest), dots (the dot grid) or checker (a transparency checkerboard). With a borderWidth, a line around it too.
settings.label: Frame

settings.means: Width of the frame around pictures in pixels: 4, 8 (the rest), 12, 16, 24 or 32. Only with a pictureFrame.
settings.label: Frame width

settings.means: The article's top picture fades into the paper: none (the rest), bottom, sides (bottom and sides) or all four edges. Architrave's page only.
settings.label: Fade first picture

settings.means: A soft shadow under the pictures, so a white screenshot stands off a white paper: none (the rest) or soft; by night a faint light edge instead. Architrave's page only.
settings.label: Picture shadow

settings.means: The pictures' corners: match (the corners every card and button has, the rest) or square (pictures cut square while cards and buttons keep theirs).
settings.label: Picture corners

settings.means: The space of the page: xcompact, compact, standard, spacious or xspacious. Standard is the rest, the theme's own. Each kind of gap moves by its own amount: inside a group a little, between items more, between sections most, so what belongs together stays together. The reading text of an article keeps its own rhythm.
settings.label: Space

settings.means: Space inside a group, a style's own: a title and the line under it, the date and the text, the padding in a button. 32 is the rest; smaller gaps of the same job follow by the same steps, and a growing gap stops at spaceSections. In px of the theme's own scale; the theme's own is the rest. On another theme the gaps move by the same number of steps along the scale (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256). On a phone the three big jobs move half as many steps. The Space dial moves all four together, one step at a time.
settings.label: Inside a group

settings.means: Space between items, a style's own: posts in a list, cards in a grid, given per side (two posts stand twice this far apart). 80 is the rest; the room above a heading moves with it. In px of the theme's own scale; the theme's own is the rest. On another theme the gaps move by the same number of steps along the scale (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256). On a phone the three big jobs move half as many steps. The Space dial moves all four together, one step at a time.
settings.label: Between items

settings.means: Space between sections, a style's own: the bands a page is stacked from, the parts at the end of an article. 64 is the rest; a shrinking gap stops at spaceInside. In px of the theme's own scale; the theme's own is the rest. On another theme the gaps move by the same number of steps along the scale (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256). On a phone the three big jobs move half as many steps. The Space dial moves all four together, one step at a time.
settings.label: Between sections

settings.means: Space above a page's title, a style's own: the room the title stands in. 96 is the rest. In px of the theme's own scale; the theme's own is the rest. On another theme the gaps move by the same number of steps along the scale (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64, 80, 96, 128, 160, 192, 256). On a phone the three big jobs move half as many steps. The Space dial moves all four together, one step at a time.
settings.label: Above the title

engine.about: The engine that draws the page, under the seven: eight roles with their members, each answering to one of the seven (presets.js engineFrom). Not saved in a record, not in the schema. Hand-kept: the block in presets.js is written from here.

keys.about: Kept by the engine and stamped as before, never in a record since the seven colours (2026-10-03): palette is the one colour pair under every style, the accent's name and the three switches the colours stand for now are worked out from them; since the layout words (2026-10-03) the article widths and the line length are worked out from titleWidth, pictureWidth, figureWidth and lineLength; since the CSS words (2026-10-03) the corners, lines and fills are worked out from radius, borderWidth, borderStyle, borderStrength and fill; since the buttons' names (2026-10-03) the buttons' colour, shape, three levels, tags' corner and current item are worked out from buttonColour, buttonShape, primaryButton, secondaryButton, tertiaryButton, tagsMatchButtons and currentItem; since the pictures' keys (2026-10-03) the picture look, frame, fade, shadow and corners are worked out from pictureFilter, colourOnHover, dimInDark, pictureFrame, frameWidth, pictureFade, pictureShadow and pictureCorners. Since the reading text's line spacing went into its role (2026-10-03) leading is the engine's dial behind roles.body.lineHeight: five steps (dense, tight, default, airy, wide for tight, snug, normal, relaxed, loose), the first paint's data-leading. Since the two fonts went into their roles (0.26.0) face and sans are the engine's keys behind roles.body.font and roles.interface.font (data-face, data-sans).
